claims.text: Increasing the Ti content in FeCoNiTi-based high-entropy alloys will shift magnetic phase transitions closer to room temperature.
Adding a small amount of an additional transition metal to FeCoNiTi-based high-entropy alloys will shift magnetic phase transitions closer to room temperature.
The proposed compositional changes will broaden the operational temperature range of the magnetocaloric effect.
Broadening and shifting the magnetic transitions will enhance the magnetocaloric effect.
The initial FeCoNiTi alloy exhibits multiple magnetic transitions.
The initial FeCoNiTi alloy has a relatively narrow magnetocaloric temperature span.
Increasing Ti and adding V or Cr can adjust magnetic interactions in the alloy.
Compositional changes will alter the alloy's lattice parameters.
Compositional changes will alter the alloy's magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
Changes in lattice parameters and magnetocrystalline anisotropy will modify exchange interactions within the alloy.
Modified magnetic interactions will shift and broaden the magnetic phase transitions.
Shifted and broadened magnetic phase transitions will enhance magnetic entropy change over a wider temperature range.
The modified alloy will exhibit a larger magnetic entropy change than unmodified FeCoNiTi.
The modified alloy will exhibit a wider magnetocaloric temperature window than unmodified FeCoNiTi.
The unmodified FeCoNiTi alloy has limited magnetocaloric performance near room temperature.
Phase separation caused by compositional adjustment may limit the proposed improvement.
Deterioration of mechanical properties may limit the proposed improvement.
The beneficial effect is expected only over a moderate range of compositional variation.
